payload.title: feat/one-history at a9963fc: a repository's stores read as one history
payload.body: Commit a9963fc on feat/one-history, from eed0938. Replay reads every tracked store of the repository as one history; a write locks the root, goes to the folder's store or its node's, and an event crossing stores is refused and rejected; aliases are local to a store; status shows the folder's store, --all the history; show G lists cites; sandbox --cut alone cuts every store. Specs, glossary, ADR 0023. Code and tests were written, and go test run, while building, before E's rubric; the rubric's checks run after it.

why: The first candidate for Q-9R7G08, with the base as its rival.
The candidate is commit a9963fc.

(a) Red on base: in a detached worktree of eed0938 with only internal/cli/history_test.go copied in, the package builds and each of the nine cli line tests fails on its own assertion, output logged. (b) Green: the ten tests pass on a9963fc. (c) Removals, one per refusal or rule, each from a9963fc in a detached worktree, diff non-empty and logged, each failing its line's test: R3 every store with .tree/events counts (drop storeOfHistory's checks and the tracked filter); R6 no duplicate-id rejection; R7a alias resolves in every store; R7b alias unique in the whole history; R7c verdict label binds in any store; R8a no crossing rule; R8b add goal with no store is not refused by name; R8c answer over two stores is not refused by name. (d) go vet ./... and go test ./... -count=1 pass on a9963fc. (e) Census: in each of the five stores under investigations/, hyp status and hyp status G for each Goal print the same bytes and exit with a9963fc's binary as with eed0938's; binaries named by sha256. (f) Line 9: with a9963fc's binary, hyp check at the repository root exits 0 with check: 0 errors, and hyp status --all there lists every Goal each of the five stores lists; command record kept. (g) A fresh subagent reviews git show a9963fc against the Goal's lines and body; its reply is saved word for word; each finding is sorted as hyp-goal-run says and does not change (a) to (f).

Line 4: a store made by hyp init that git does not track yet reads only itself, so its first Goal cannot cite a key of another store (unknown node, exit 2), nor name another store's id in its text (review finding 1).

Line 2: hyp status --all and hyp status G-id, run in a folder whose store adds nothing to the history (a testdata store, a trial store under .tree/evidence, an untracked store), read only that store (review finding 2).

Line 8: no test refuses or rejects a select, or a checkpoint refer, whose node or key lies in another store, and the write-time cases check only exit 1, not that the refusal names the crossing rule (review finding 3).
Line 4: the refusals of a cross-store cite and reading-of that are not settled are tested by exit 1 only, not by the not-settled message (review finding 4).

limits: Line 2: hyp status G-id --as-of REF, run in a folder whose store adds nothing to the history, resolves REF in that store alone and exits 2 with unknown node (review finding 2).

Line 5: a repository whose one tracked store is at its root locks that store's .tree/events, while a writer in an untracked store below it locks the repository root, so their appends are not serialized (review finding 4).
readings: Line 3: "adds nothing to the history" has two meanings. Meaning 1: a store git does not track adds nothing to the history read from any folder, also its own. Meaning 2: it adds nothing to the history read from other folders, but read from its own folder it joins the history. This run used meaning 2. TestCiteAcrossStores tests meaning 2; one-history-1 fails it. Example: after hyp init in investigations/c, hyp add goal --cite 1=G-A#1 there passes with meaning 2 and is unknown node with meaning 1. Question: may a new untracked store read the other stores from its own folder?

Line 8: "it is appended to the store that holds its node" has two meanings. Meaning 1: hyp writes the event to the store of its node, from any folder. Meaning 2: hyp writes the event to the store of the current folder, and refuses it with exit 1 when its node is in another store. This run used meaning 2. TestEventNeverCrossesStores tests meaning 2; no candidate fails it. Example: in store a's folder, hyp add dq --parent <a Goal of store b> is refused with meaning 2 and written to store b with meaning 1. Question: must a write in one store's folder go to another store?

why: Pre-registered rubric: (a) to (g) hold, so one-history-2 is supported; the review's cases of lines are limits.

limits: Lines 3 and 6: a tracked store reached from a folder through a symbolic link, or through a path in another letter case on a file system that ignores case, joins the history a second time as an untracked store, so replay rejects each of its events as a duplicate id (review finding 1).

Line 5: a writer in a tracked store does not read a store that git does not track yet, so two appends to the two stores in one millisecond can sort against the order in which they took the lock (review finding 5).
readings: Line 6: "rejected on replay at the later line" has two meanings. Meaning 1: of two lines with one id, hyp rejects the later line in merge order, also when it rejects the earlier line for another rule. Meaning 2: hyp rejects a line whose id an applied event holds; when the earlier line is rejected for another rule, the later line applies. This run used meaning 2. TestDuplicateIDAcrossStores tests only lines that both apply. Example: store b holds a copy of a's question line that sorts first and crosses stores; with meaning 2, a's line applies. Question: must hyp reject store a's line here too?
